# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Li_2017_voriconazole"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Li_2017_voriconazole"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1097/FTD.0000000000000425> (open access, PMC5538305)

# Population

Li 2017 is a retrospective therapeutic-drug-monitoring study of adult renal
transplant recipients who received voriconazole for prevention or treatment of
invasive fungal infection at the Department of Urological Organ
Transplantation, Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University (Changsha,
China), between September 2015 and June 2016 (Methods, "Patients and Data
Collection"). Patients aged 15 years or younger, patients on a strong CYP2C19
inducer (e.g. rifampin), and patients with substantial missing data were
excluded.

The analysis used 125 trough concentrations (Cmin, drawn 30 minutes before the
next dose; median 2.18, range 0.16-9.59 ug/mL) from 56 patients (Results,
"Patient Demographics and Dose Characteristics"). Table 1 reports 39 men and 17
women (30.4% female), age 40 +/- 8 years (18-60), weight 55 +/- 10 kg (33-78),
AST 33.0 +/- 48.1 U/L (7.9-311.5) and creatinine clearance 51.8 +/- 24.7 mL/min.
CYP2C19 phenotypes were 2 rapid metabolizers (RM, `*1/*17`), 24 extensive
metabolizers (EM, `*1/*1`), 25 intermediate metabolizers (IM, `*1/*2`, `*1/*3`,
`*2/*17`) and 5 poor metabolizers (PM, `*2/*2`) (Tables 1 and 3). 78.6% of
patients were within the first year after transplantation; 46.4% received a
proton pump inhibitor and 69.6% a glucocorticoid. The usual starting regimen was
200 mg twice daily, adjusted after the first trough; intravenous and oral forms
were both used.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Li_2017_voriconazole")$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment model, first-order absorption and elimination | n/a | Methods, "Structural Model"; Results, "Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis" |
| `lka` (ka, fixed) | 1.1 1/h | Methods, "Structural Model" ("fixed to a value of 1.1 h", refs 18-20) |
| `lcl` (theta_CL, CL at AST = 33 U/L) | 4.76 L/h | Table 5 (final model); Table 4; Abstract |
| `lvc` (theta_V, V for the RM reference) | 22.47 L | Table 5 (final model); Table 4; Abstract |
| `e_cyp2c19_em_vc` (theta_1) | 2.21 | Table 5 |
| `e_cyp2c19_im_vc` (theta_2) | 4.67 | Table 5 |
| `e_cyp2c19_pm_vc` (theta_3) | 3.30 | Table 5 |
| `e_ast_cl` (theta_4) | -0.23 | Table 5; Abstract equation `(AST/33)^(-0.23)` |
| V = theta_V x [1 + theta_1 (EM=1)] x [1 + theta_2 (IM=1)] x [1 + theta_3 (PM=1)] x exp(eta_V) | n/a | Table 5 footnote; Results and Abstract |
| CL = theta_CL x (AST/33)^theta_4 x exp(eta_CL) | n/a | Table 5 footnote; Results and Abstract |
| `etalvc` | 0.9604 (omega_V = 0.98 SD) | Table 5; Abstract prints the variance exp(0.96) |
| `etalcl` | 0.1369 (omega_CL = 0.37 SD) | Table 5; Abstract prints the variance exp(0.14) |
| `propSd` | 0.39 | Table 5 sigma; Results prints the variance as `Cobs = Cpred x (1 + 0.15)` |
| Exponential IIV, proportional residual error | n/a | Methods, "Statistical Model" (equations 2 and 4); Results |

```{r typical-volumes}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Li_2017_voriconazole"))
p <- mod$theta
phenotype_levels <- c("RM", "EM", "IM", "PM")

phenotypes <- tibble::tibble(
  phenotype = c("RM", "EM", "IM", "PM"),
  CYP2C19_RM = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 0L),
  CYP2C19_IM = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 0L),
  CYP2C19_PM = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 1L),
  CYP2C19_UM = 0L
)

typical <- phenotypes |>
  mutate(
    V = exp(p[["lvc"]]) *
      (1 + p[["e_cyp2c19_em_vc"]] * (1 - CYP2C19_RM - CYP2C19_IM - CYP2C19_PM - CYP2C19_UM)) *
      (1 + p[["e_cyp2c19_im_vc"]] * CYP2C19_IM) *
      (1 + p[["e_cyp2c19_pm_vc"]] * CYP2C19_PM),
    CL = exp(p[["lcl"]]),
    `t1/2 (h)` = log(2) * V / CL
  )

# The phenotype volumes the Table 5 equation gives, written out by hand.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  typical$V,
  22.47 * c(1, 1 + 2.21, 1 + 4.67, 1 + 3.30)
)))

typical |>
  select(phenotype, V, CL, `t1/2 (h)`) |>
  dplyr::rename("CYP2C19 phenotype" = phenotype, "V (L)" = V, "CL (L/h)" = CL) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value volume, clearance and half-life by CYP2C19 phenotype at AST = 33 U/L.")
```

# Virtual cohort

The original data are not public. The cohort below has 50 subjects in each of
the four phenotype strata the model resolves (RM, EM, IM, PM). AST is drawn from
a log-normal distribution with the Table 1 mean and SD (33.0 and 48.1 U/L),
keeping only draws inside the observed 7.9-311.5 U/L range (draws outside are
redrawn rather than clipped, so the range does not pile subjects at its
limits).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20170422)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170422)

n_per_arm <- 50L

draw_ast <- function(n, mean = 33.0, sd = 48.1, lo = 7.9, hi = 311.5) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (sd / mean)^2))
  meanlog <- log(mean) - sdlog^2 / 2
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rlnorm(n, meanlog, sdlog)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

cohort <- phenotypes |>
  slice(rep(seq_len(n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), AST = draw_ast(n()))
```

# Simulation

Every subject receives oral 200 mg twice daily, the usual regimen of the study,
simulated directly at steady state (`ss = 1`) because the slow-eliminating
subjects (large `eta_V`) would otherwise need several weeks of run-in. The
observation grid covers one 12-hour dosing interval, so the value at time 0 is
the steady-state trough.

```{r simulate}
tau <- 12
dose <- 200
obs_times <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)

covs <- cohort |> select(id, phenotype, AST, CYP2C19_RM, CYP2C19_IM, CYP2C19_PM, CYP2C19_UM)

ev_ss <- bind_rows(
  covs |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = tau, ss = 1L),
  covs |> tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = NA_real_, ss = NA_integer_)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_ss, keep = "phenotype", maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_ss$Cc))
```

## Steady-state profiles by phenotype

```{r fig-profiles}
sim_ss |>
  mutate(phenotype = factor(phenotype, levels = phenotype_levels)) |>
  group_by(phenotype, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1, 5.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~phenotype, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Voriconazole (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles, 200 mg every 12 h orally. Dashed lines: the 1.0-5.5 ug/mL window the paper used."
  )
```

## Troughs against the observed Table 3 means

Li 2017 does not publish a simulation or NCA table. Its Table 3 reports the
observed mean (SD) trough by phenotype, which reflects doses that were adjusted
after the first trough, so the comparison below is descriptive, not a fit
criterion. The paper itself reports that the final model's population
prediction deviates at high concentrations (Discussion).

```{r troughs}
observed_t3 <- tibble::tibble(
  phenotype = c("RM", "EM", "IM", "PM"),
  obs_mean = c(0.40, 1.76, 3.02, 4.43),
  obs_sd = c(0.14, 1.24, 2.07, 2.46)
)

troughs <- sim_ss |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  group_by(phenotype) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(Cc), sim_mean = mean(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(observed_t3, by = "phenotype") |>
  arrange(factor(phenotype, levels = phenotype_levels))

troughs |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CYP2C19 phenotype" = phenotype,
    "Simulated median Cmin" = sim_median,
    "Simulated mean Cmin" = sim_mean,
    "Observed mean Cmin (Table 3)" = obs_mean,
    "Observed SD (Table 3)" = obs_sd
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Steady-state trough (ug/mL) at 200 mg every 12 h versus the observed Table 3 means.")
```

The typical-value troughs (below) order the phenotypes RM < EM < PM < IM. The
observed means order RM < EM < IM < PM, with the PM mean resting on 5 patients.
Because CYP2C19 enters the model only through V and clearance does not depend on
phenotype, every phenotype has the same exposure (AUC = Dose/CL) at a given
dose; the trough differences come entirely from the slower elimination that a
larger V gives.

## Deterministic checks

The typical-value steady-state trough of a one-compartment model with
first-order absorption has a closed form; the rxode2 solve must match it, and
the phenotype ordering it implies is checked here rather than on the random
cohort.

```{r typical-checks}
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  phenotypes |> mutate(id = seq_len(n()), AST = 33, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L,
                       cmt = "depot", ii = tau, ss = 1L),
  phenotypes |> mutate(id = seq_len(n()), AST = 33) |> tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 6, 12)) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = NA_real_, ss = NA_integer_)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ, keep = "phenotype",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  as.data.frame()

ka <- exp(p[["lka"]])
closed_form <- function(t, V, CL) {
  k <- CL / V
  dose * ka / (V * (ka - k)) *
    (exp(-k * t) / (1 - exp(-k * tau)) - exp(-ka * t) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))
}

chk <- sim_typ |>
  left_join(typical |> select(phenotype, V, CL), by = "phenotype") |>
  mutate(cf = closed_form(time, V, CL))
# Same parameters on both sides: the difference is integrator error only.
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$Cc / chk$cf - 1)) < 1e-6)

typ_trough <- chk |> filter(time == 0) |> arrange(factor(phenotype, levels = phenotype_levels))
stopifnot(
  typ_trough$Cc[typ_trough$phenotype == "RM"] < typ_trough$Cc[typ_trough$phenotype == "EM"],
  typ_trough$Cc[typ_trough$phenotype == "EM"] < typ_trough$Cc[typ_trough$phenotype == "PM"],
  typ_trough$Cc[typ_trough$phenotype == "PM"] < typ_trough$Cc[typ_trough$phenotype == "IM"]
)
typ_trough |>
  select(phenotype, Cc) |>
  dplyr::rename("CYP2C19 phenotype" = phenotype, "Typical Cmin,ss (ug/mL)" = Cc) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# PKNCA validation

## Single-dose typical values

For a single 200 mg oral dose the typical AUC0-inf is Dose / CL = 200 / 4.76 =
42.0 mg h/L in every phenotype, and the terminal half-life is log(2) V / CL. The
observation grid runs to 400 h so the IM half-life (18.6 h) is well resolved.

```{r nca-single}
sd_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, seq(36, 400, by = 12))))
ev_sd <- bind_rows(
  phenotypes |> mutate(id = seq_len(n()), AST = 33, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  phenotypes |> mutate(id = seq_len(n()), AST = 33) |> tidyr::crossing(time = sd_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_sd, keep = "phenotype",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(phenotype))

# The RM profile (t1/2 3.3 h) reaches integrator noise long before 400 h;
# drop the numerically-zero tail after the peak so lambda-z is not fitted to
# it.
stopifnot(all(sim_sd$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_sd$Cc, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
conc_sd <- sim_sd |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_sd <- ev_sd |> filter(evid == 1) |> mutate(treatment = as.character(phenotype)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

nca_sd <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_sd, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_sd, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

sd_res <- as.data.frame(nca_sd$result) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(typical |> mutate(treatment = as.character(phenotype)) |>
              select(treatment, V, CL), by = "treatment")

# AUC0-inf * CL == Dose and half-life == log(2) V / CL (one subject per
# phenotype, deterministic): the bounds sit well above trapezoid and
# lambda-z fitting error on this grid.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sd_res$aucinf.obs * sd_res$CL / dose - 1)) < 0.02,
  max(abs(sd_res$half.life / (log(2) * sd_res$V / sd_res$CL) - 1)) < 0.02
)

sd_res |>
  arrange(factor(treatment, levels = phenotype_levels)) |>
  select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CYP2C19 phenotype" = treatment, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (mg h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value NCA after a single 200 mg oral dose (AST = 33 U/L).")
```

## Steady-state cohort

```{r nca-ss}
conc_ss <- sim_ss |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(phenotype), Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_ss <- ev_ss |> filter(evid == 1) |> mutate(treatment = as.character(phenotype)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

nca_ss <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

ss_res <- as.data.frame(nca_ss$result) |>
  select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(sim_ss |> filter(time == 0) |> select(id, cl), by = "id")

# At steady state AUCtau * CL == Dose per subject. Large eta_V subjects have a
# flat profile and fast-absorbing small-V subjects a narrow peak, so the
# trapezoid error is checked on the centre and a robust quantile.
pct_err <- 100 * (ss_res$auclast * ss_res$cl / dose - 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(pct_err)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(pct_err), 0.9) < 5
)

ss_res |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    across(c(cmax, cmin, auclast), median),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(factor(treatment, levels = phenotype_levels)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CYP2C19 phenotype" = treatment, "Median Cmax,ss (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "Median Cmin,ss (ug/mL)" = cmin, "Median AUCtau,ss (mg h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Steady-state NCA (200 mg every 12 h orally), stochastic cohort, 50 subjects per phenotype.")
```

Li 2017 reports no NCA parameters, so there is no published NCA table to
compare against.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Reference category for V.** Li 2017's equation multiplies `theta_V` by a
  factor for each of EM, IM and PM, so its reference phenotype is the rapid
  metabolizer (`*1/*17`, 2 patients). The model keeps that parameterization and
  the paper's estimates. It takes the register indicators `CYP2C19_RM`,
  `CYP2C19_IM`, `CYP2C19_PM` and `CYP2C19_UM` and derives the extensive
  metabolizer as the subject flagged by none of them, so every subject needs
  exactly one phenotype coded (all four 0 means EM).
* **Ultrarapid metabolizers.** The paper defines a UM (`*17/*17`) category but
  enrolled no UM patients. The model gives UM the rapid-metabolizer V (the
  other `*17` gain-of-function group) instead of the EM V; this is an
  extrapolation outside the fitted cohort.
* **Absorption and route.** ka was fixed at 1.1 (the text prints the unit as
  "h"; the rate constant is per hour) and no bioavailability was estimated.
  Both intravenous and oral forms were given in the study, but the paper does
  not say how intravenous doses were entered in the first-order-absorption
  model. CL and V are therefore apparent values for oral dosing (F taken as 1);
  an intravenous dose can be given into `central`, which treats F as 1 as
  well.
* **IIV and residual scale.** Tables 4 and 5 print omega and sigma in a column
  pair whose second column is labelled "SD" (the uncertainty of the estimate).
  The omega and sigma estimates are themselves SDs: the Abstract's final
  equation prints `exp(0.96)` and `exp(0.14)`, and the Results print the
  residual model as `Cpred x (1 + 0.15)`, which are 0.98^2, 0.37^2 and 0.39^2.
  The model uses variances 0.9604 and 0.1369 and a proportional SD of 0.39. No
  covariance between eta_V and eta_CL was reported, so the omega matrix is
  diagonal.
* **AST.** The reference value 33 U/L is the Table 1 cohort mean. The paper
  does not say whether AST was entered per sample or per patient.
* **Errata and supplements.** A search of Europe PMC and PubMed on 2026-11-25
  found no erratum or correction, and the article has no supplementary
  material.
